label: copy-phase input c (echoed c fed back) in short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L) when the fed-back input token is the letter c (99.8% of activation mass on in_tok == c). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, including on c tokens there, and almost never on other copy-phase inputs. Magnitude is largest for short sequences (L = 3-5) and early recall positions: the top activations are the c right after <DEL> + first token (e.g. k c a <DEL> k [c]). It falls off as L and recall_idx grow, and a c that is a repeat, or is far into the copy, gives weak activations or none. In long sequences (L >= 7) or with many outputs still to go, copy-phase c inputs mostly stay inactive. The bare token rule (copy-phase c) gets recall 0.98 but precision only 0.29. Gating on L <= 6 and to_go <= 3 raises dev F1 to 0.79 (P 0.75, R 0.85, mass 0.96), so the length dependence is graded rather than a clean cutoff.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: c, f, a, q, t, w; least: 0, b, s, l) and the token being output (most: c, a, w, t, d, v; least: 1, h, m, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, recall_idx=3, L=3 & t=5.
